Alex K: ran an nsys capture on the nightly matmul regression, attaching the trace link -> https://perf.redwood/runs/1952103333/nsv
Alex K: initial quick read: long streaks of cublasLt::gemm kernel launches separated by small host->device memcpy spikes. looks like workspace churn between launches.
perf-bot: automated alert: regression detected on nightly matmul benchmark. p99 latency +12% vs baseline (shape sweep: B=1..8, S=128..1024). See nsys summary.
Maria L: can you paste the nsys cmd and the nvtx regions you used? will try to open trace locally.
Alex K: command i used:
```
nsys profile --output=/tmp/matmul_nsys --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn,osrt,nvtx --sample=none --duration=120 --stats=true python -m infra.bench.matmul_sweep
```
Alex K: nvtx regions: MATMUL_FORWARD / kv_cache_lookup / apply_attention / emit_tokens
Vikram S: curious if this is kv-cache induced — KV cache writes during the prefix warmup could be changing stride/layout and forcing different cuBLASLt workspace selections.
Sophie N: any nvprof/perfetto timelines showing workspace allocation events? those usually show up as cudaMalloc/cudaFree flurries.
Alex K: yes — perfetto timeline shows cudaMalloc peaks right before a block of gemm kernels. also lots of small memcpy D2D.
Alex K: snippet from the nsys event log (condensed):
```
[0.12s] cublasLt:chooseAlgo(shape=(8,1024,1024)) -> algo=7 workspace=256KB
[0.13s] cudaMemcpyAsync (host->device) size=128KB
[0.14s] cublasLt:launch(algo=7)
[0.16s] cublasLt:chooseAlgo(shape=(8,1024,1024)) -> algo=12 workspace=1.5MB
[0.17s] cublasLt:allocWorkspace(1.5MB)
[0.18s] cublasLt:launch(algo=12)
[0.19s] cublasLt:freeWorkspace
```
Maria L: that alternating algo+workspace pattern smells like heuristics flipping based on transient tensor strides (maybe due to batched vs padded shapes).
Vikram S: also saw kernel time heatmap — algo=7 is fast but suffers when workspace < threshold, then chooseAlgo picks algo=12 which needs larger workspace and adds alloc/free overhead.
Alex K: reproduced locally with controlled shapes: when we pin KVCACHE enabled, workspace stable -> consistent algo (7) and latency drops ~10%.
Sophie N: good repro. can you try forcing algo=7 via cublasLt attributes to see raw kernel time without allocator noise?
Alex K: plan: (1) force algo=7 + no workspace alloc (2) run perfetto and nsys side-by-side (3) bisect KV cache changes since last good commit
perf-bot: perf job queued: INF-BENCH-1952 (nsys+perfetto) — results in ~45m
Maria L: another angle: batching heuristic might be emitting inconsistent batch sizes from the runtime when KV cache hits/misses change sequence length distribution.
Vikram S: yep. if the runtime packs requests differently between warm and steady state you can get alternating small/large batches which then lead to different algorithm picks.
Sophie N: quick mitigation we can try: add a per-worker stable workspace pool so cublasLt alloc/free churn is amortized.
Alex K: filed INF-421: "matmul workspace churn after KV cache warmup" with trace links and initial findings. I'll run the forced-algo experiment and post results here.
Maria L: thanks — if you share the perfetto link I can annotate the timeline and highlight malloc hotspots.
Alex K: will post perfetto trace in ~30m. tagging @Sophie N and @Vikram S for follow-ups. :mag:
